decisions.title: What this year is for
decisions.description: The chief executive wants to know what will be different by December, and what you are leaving alone to get it.
decisions.context: A second year starts with what the first one left: risks named and not treated, a team that carried the winter, and whatever is still being built. It cannot do all three at full strength.

options.label: Deliver before starting more
options.description: Put the year behind delivery: whatever is running, or the first thing you start, lands before anything else begins.
visibleKnownEffects: Nothing new starts until the running work lands

immediateEffects.reason: You promised to finish what you had started.

options.label: Take on the largest untreated risk
options.description: Name the risk nobody has treated and make it the year's work.
visibleKnownEffects: The board hears a risk named
Anything already running waits its turn

immediateEffects.reason: You named the year's work by the risk it treats.

options.label: Rebuild the team first
options.description: Spend the first months, and some of the money, on the people who will do the rest.
visibleKnownEffects: Delivery is slower for a while

immediateEffects.reason: She asked about outcomes and heard about the team.

decisions.title: The Kestrel boundary, again
decisions.description: The boundary around Kestrel Digital has held since the network join. The CFO wants it down so this year's synergy number can land early.
decisions.context: Holding it through peak cost nothing that showed. Holding it now delays the integration the business is counting on this year.

options.label: Lift it now
options.description: Let the integration and the savings go ahead.
visibleKnownEffects: Kestrel's estate joins the corporate network

immediateEffects.reason: You lifted the Kestrel boundary in January.

options.label: Lift it after a scoped review
options.description: Two weeks of architecture time on what crosses the boundary, then lift it.
visibleKnownEffects: The savings slip by a few weeks

options.label: Keep it until the integration is done
options.description: Integrate Kestrel's services one at a time through the boundary.
visibleKnownEffects: The CFO will take it to the chief executive
Integration takes most of the year

immediateEffects.reason: You kept the Kestrel boundary into a second year.

decisions.title: Switching enforcement on
decisions.description: Enforcement of the second factor and the privileged access flow was put off until after peak trading. Peak is over.
decisions.context: Every week it waits, the exception list grows. Every week it is on, somebody senior finds out they never enrolled.

options.label: Switch it on next week
options.description: Standing exceptions expire and anyone without the second factor enrols or is locked out.
visibleKnownEffects: A noisy week for the service desk
The control means what it says

immediateEffects.reason: You switched enforcement on in January.

options.label: Give the business another month
options.description: Write to every exception holder and switch on in February.

immediateEffects.reason: You gave the business another month before enforcement.

decisions.title: The production restore test
decisions.description: The restore test deferred from last year needs four hours of payments on a Sunday morning. Operations can offer one window this month.
decisions.context: Recovery that has never been run is a plan. The only way to find out is the window, and the window costs payments either way.

options.label: Take the window
options.description: Restore Nexora Pay in production, on a Sunday morning, this month.
visibleKnownEffects: The first real evidence of recovery

immediateEffects.reason: You took four hours of payments for a restore test.

options.label: Restore into the test tenancy
options.description: Prove the backups restore, without touching production.

options.label: Defer it to the spring
options.description: Wait for a quieter window.
visibleKnownEffects: Recovery stays a plan for another season

immediateEffects.reason: The restore test was deferred a second time.

decisions.title: What to send the regulator
decisions.description: The regulator wants last year's post-incident review and evidence that its actions were completed. Some of the actions are still open.
decisions.context: The review was written to be honest internally. What goes to the regulator will be read against what was said at the time, and kept.

options.label: Send it as written, open actions marked
options.description: The review, unedited, with a dated plan for what is not done.

immediateEffects.reason: You sent the regulator the review as written.

options.label: Close the open actions first, then send
options.description: A month of engineering effort so the evidence is complete when it goes.
visibleKnownEffects: The submission is late but complete

immediateEffects.reason: You closed the actions before writing to the regulator.

options.label: Send a summary
options.description: A shorter document that covers what they asked.
visibleKnownEffects: The regulator decides whether it is enough

decisions.title: The customer service assistant
decisions.description: Operations wants an AI assistant reading case histories, order records and customer messages on every agent's desktop by the autumn.
decisions.context: The assistant sees what the agent sees, and agents see a great deal. What it is allowed to read, and what it keeps, are decided now or not at all.

options.label: Sign after a data protection assessment
options.description: Six weeks of work on what it can read and what it keeps, then roll it out.

immediateEffects.reason: You held the assistant for an assessment.

options.label: Sign as it stands
options.description: Let operations roll it out on the supplier's terms.
visibleKnownEffects: Operations gets what it asked for
Nobody has looked at what it reads

immediateEffects.reason: You backed the assistant without conditions.

options.label: Pilot it with one team first
options.description: One team for two months, then decide.
visibleKnownEffects: You find out what it does before everybody has it

immediateEffects.reason: You asked for a pilot before the roll-out.

decisions.title: Who decides in seventy-two hours
decisions.description: From October a significant incident must be reported within seventy-two hours. Today nobody owns the decision, so nobody can say how long it would take.
decisions.context: A deadline the organisation has never met is a finding waiting to happen. Who owns the decision matters more than the template.

options.label: Build the process, with a named decision-maker
options.description: Write it, name who decides, and exercise it against a realistic incident.

immediateEffects.reason: You built the reporting process with her.

options.label: Make yourself the decision-maker
options.description: You decide whether an incident is significant, and legal reports it.
visibleKnownEffects: It lands on you at three in the morning

immediateEffects.reason: You took the reporting decision yourself.

options.label: Leave it with legal, case by case
options.description: Legal handles each incident as it comes.

immediateEffects.reason: You left the seventy-two-hour decision with legal.
